incident-bot: [ALERT] Latency SLO p95 breach detected for policy smart-route-us-east at 2026-03-15T17:02:14Z. Automated fallback to model-compact-eu triggered. Rolling reroutes observed.

mike (oncall): Paging in. I'm on it. /assign

raj (infra): I see a spike in p95 tokens on us-east serving cluster. CPU stable but queue depth jumped. Logs show many short-lived fallbacks.

emily (sre-eng): Can you paste the routing decision trace? Might be policy oscillation between cost-tier and latency-tier.

ops-runner-bot: Routing trace for request sample id abc123:
```
policy evaluate -> us-east primary (p95=220ms) -> fallback to eu-west-compact (p95_est=140ms) -> back to us-east after cooldown expired -> repeated every ~45s
```

sara (ml): Looks like model-compact-eu variant has different seq len characteristics; KV cache warmup is poor causing eu-west latency to initially be better then degrade.

mike (oncall): Customer impact? Any errors or just latency? @sara @raj

raj (infra): No increased 5xxs. It's latency-only but causes repeated region hops; that increases tail latency for affected requests. We've got ~2% of routed traffic bouncing in last 10m.

mike (oncall): Ok mitigations: 1) disable automated region fallback for smart-route-us-east (turn off policy 'region-fallback') 2) scale us-east pool by +2 GPUs 3) open incident bridge if threshold persists. I'll make the policy change now.

raj (infra): Policy change applied: `region-fallback=false` for smart-route-us-east. Confirming via config API.

ops-runner-bot: Config update accepted. New policy snapshot id: cfg-20260315-001

sara (ml): Also recommend pinning to model-latency-stable variant for 10m while we observe. Suggest `model_variant=stable-v2`.

mike (oncall): Pinned variant to stable-v2 for smart-route-us-east. Monitoring.

emily (sre-eng): Seeing immediate reduction in reroutes. p95 falling back toward normal but still slightly elevated. Any customer-facing alerts? We should notify CSMs.

mike (oncall): I'll notify CSMs and mark incident as 'investigating' in the tracker. Quick blameless postmortem steps: why did cooldown logic allow bounce? Who owns policy thresholds?

raj (infra): Opening a follow-up ticket: infra#987 - routing cooldowns not preventing oscillation for mixed-variant pools.

sara (ml): I'll run eval on compact vs stable variant under mixed load and KV warmup. Tagging ml-team.

mike (oncall): Timeline: 17:02 alert -> 17:04 policy disable -> 17:06 variant pin -> 17:08 p95 stabilized. Moving to monitoring. If p95 rises again, escalate to SEV.

emily (sre-eng): Thanks all. I'll collect logs for the postmortem. :thumbsup:

ops-runner-bot: Incident update logged to #incidents: incident-1934561234. No errors recorded, latency-only. Customers with active requests in window: account-445, account-992 (2% of their calls experienced reroute-induced latency of +300ms on average).

mike (oncall): Closing loop: will handoff to raj for infra follow-up and sara for variant evaluation. Handoff note: oncall->raj at 17:15 UTC. /handoff

raj (infra): Ack. Taking ownership of infra ticket. Will propose cooldown/backoff tuning and a simulation harness.

sara (ml): Ack. Will produce perf matrix and recommend default variant settings.

mike (oncall): Incident moved to post-incident review, paging cleared. :white_check_mark:
